name: birth

attributes.attribute: a mythic theme among the Celts
source of protective waters for childbirth

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Birth is a mythic theme among the Celts. Fertility was never taken for granted. The Celts recorded many invocations and rituals to raise it. Those records show real concern. Birth itself carried danger. Protective rites for safe childbirth included drinking holy well waters. Some wore clothing dipped in those waters. Many wells also had oracular roles. Parents-to-be likely consulted them about the child.

okr.objective: Describe birth as a mythic theme and the rituals that surrounded it.
key_results: Fertility was never taken for granted by the Celts.
Many recorded invocations and rituals sought to increase it.
Protective rites for childbirth used holy well waters.
Parents-to-be likely consulted oracular wells about the child.
